test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 7 hours and 10 hours, respectively, and pipe C can empty the full tank in 14 hours. All three pipes are opened together, but pipe A is closed after 4.5 hours. In how many hours will the remaining part of tank be filled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work (LCM of 7, 10, 14)** = 70 units.

Efficiencies: A = 10, B = 7, C = −5. Combined (A+B+C) = 10 + 7 − 5 = 12 units/hr.

Work done in 4.5 hours = 12 × 4.5 = 54 units.

Remaining work = 70 − 54 = 16 units. Combined (B+C) = 7 − 5 = 2 units/hr.

Remaining time = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe A fills in 7 hrs, Pipe B in 10 hrs, Pipe C empties in 14 hrs. A is closed after 4.5 hrs.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Sign Convention

Inlet pipes (filling) are taken as **positive efficiency**, while outlet pipes (emptying/leakage) are taken as **negative efficiency**.

Work done by multiple pipes

Total part filled in 1 hour = (1/A) + (1/B) − (1/C), where A and B are inlet and C is an outlet pipe.

Total Time Calculation

If the question asks for **total time**, add the initial 4.5 hours to the remaining 8 hours (Total = 12.5 hours).</p
